football_evidence.question: Can Texas Tech take away West Virginia’s big plays?
football_evidence.assessment: EdgeDesk’s number is 2.1 points closer to West Virginia than the line, and EdgeDesk cannot account for most of that: its own breakdown accounts for about 0.0 of the 2.1 points. The measured football evidence leans toward Texas Tech, not toward EdgeDesk’s number. Treat the gap as an open research question, not as an edge.
supporting: When West Virginia has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): West Virginia’s offense averages 10.3 yards per pass attempt, and Texas Tech’s defense allows 7.5 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).

When West Virginia has the ball (big plays through the air): West Virginia’s offense turns 20.3% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Texas Tech’s defense gives up explosive gains on 6.6% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When West Virginia has the ball (third down): West Virginia’s offense converts 50.7% of its third downs, and Texas Tech’s defense allows opponents to convert 36.7% of their third downs (FBS average 39.6%).
In his last two games (Arizona State and Arizona), Castellanos averaged 6.2 yards per attempt, against 7.9 in his three games before that.
contradicting: When Texas Tech has the ball (big plays through the air): Texas Tech’s offense turns 8.7% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and West Virginia’s defense gives up explosive gains on 18.3% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Texas Tech has the ball (big plays on the ground): Texas Tech’s offense turns 9.7% of its runs into explosive gains, and West Virginia’s defense gives up explosive gains on 7.9% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When West Virginia has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): West Virginia’s offense has allowed a sack on 8.4% of its dropbacks, and Texas Tech’s defense sacks the quarterback on 6.1% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Texas Tech has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Texas Tech’s offense averages 7.2 yards per pass attempt, and West Virginia’s defense allows 10.3 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).
quarterbacks: Will Hammond has completed 136 of 204 passes (66.7%) for 1,541 yards, 7.6 yards per attempt, 6 touchdowns and 6 interceptions in seven games for Texas Tech, and has been sacked on 12 of 216 dropbacks.
Thomas Castellanos has completed 17 of 32 passes (53.1%) for 209 yards, 6.5 yards per attempt, 4 touchdowns and 1 interception in five games for Texas Tech, and has been sacked on 2 of 34 dropbacks.

Michael Hawkins Jr. has completed 90 of 159 passes (56.6%) for 1,598 yards, 10.1 yards per attempt, 11 touchdowns and 2 interceptions in eight games for West Virginia, and has been sacked on 15 of 174 dropbacks.
